metadata.title: Why Seek Therapy in Antibes | Karen Schenck
metadata.description: Anxiety, professional burnout, relationship difficulties, life transitions: discover the main reasons people start therapy and how it can help.

whyConsultPage.title: Why seek therapy?
whyConsultPage.intro: It isn't always easy to know when it's time to see a therapist. Some difficulties follow a specific life event. Others build up gradually, or feel like they keep repeating despite your efforts to move past them. Anxiety, professional exhaustion, relationship difficulties or periods of transition can affect your personal, family or professional life. Below are the main reasons that lead people to seek therapy.

motifs.title: Anxiety
motifs.teaser: Worries take up more and more space.
motifs.intro: Worries take up more and more space. You find it hard to stop thinking, to relax, or to get restorative sleep. You often feel on edge, without always understanding why. Over time, this constant state of tension can become overwhelming and affect your personal, professional and relational life.
motifs.whenText: When these difficulties become hard to manage alone, or take up more and more space in your daily life, therapy can help you understand the mechanisms at play and regain a better balance.
motifs.supportText: The goal isn't just to ease symptoms. It's also about identifying the mechanisms that maintain them, in order to support lasting change.
motifs.imageAlt: Line-art illustration of a figure holding their head in their hands, surrounded by a tangle of thoughts, over navy and terracotta shapes

motifs.title: Professional burnout
motifs.teaser: You feel like you have no energy left.
motifs.intro: You feel like you have no energy left, even for the simplest tasks. Fatigue no longer goes away with rest. You struggle to concentrate, feel overwhelmed, irritable or unmotivated. What used to come naturally is becoming increasingly difficult. Burnout can gradually affect your health, relationships and quality of life.
motifs.whenText: When exhaustion settles in and everyday life becomes hard to manage, therapy can help you understand what led to this situation and gradually regain your footing.
motifs.supportText: The goal isn't only to support recovery. It's about identifying the factors that contributed to the exhaustion, to support a lasting recovery and reduce the risk of it happening again.
motifs.imageAlt: Line-art illustration of a seated figure, head lowered and shoulders slumped, over navy and terracotta shapes

motifs.title: Relationship difficulties
motifs.teaser: You feel like you keep reliving the same situations.
motifs.intro: You feel like you keep reliving the same situations despite your efforts to change things. Conflicts repeat themselves, and it becomes hard to set boundaries, find your place in a relationship, or build peaceful connections. Certain experiences can also weaken trust in yourself or in others. Over time, these difficulties can weigh on your emotional balance and on different areas of your life.
motifs.whenText: When these difficulties become recurring or cause lasting distress, therapy can help you better understand what is happening and build more balanced relationships.
motifs.supportText: Therapeutic work makes it possible to explore the relational patterns that keep repeating, better understand their origin, and develop new ways of relating to yourself and to others.
motifs.imageAlt: Line-art illustration of two figures standing back to back, separated by a terracotta leaf, over slate blue and beige shapes

motifs.title: Life transitions
motifs.teaser: Certain events disrupt the bearings you built over time.
motifs.intro: Certain events disrupt the bearings you built over time. Life is marked by major stages that we go through more or less easily. They can raise questions and doubts, but also a deep sense of uncertainty or sadness. These periods of transition sometimes take time before a new balance is found.
motifs.whenText: When these changes become difficult to go through, or cause lasting distress, therapy can help you move forward with more serenity.
motifs.supportText: Therapy offers a space to put words to what you are experiencing, better integrate this period of your life, and find bearings suited to your situation.
motifs.imageAlt: Illustration of a winding path through navy, sand and terracotta hills toward a pale sun, with a line-art seedling

practicePage.title: My practice
practicePage.intro: I don't believe a single method can respond to every situation. That is why I chose to combine several complementary therapeutic approaches, drawn on according to your needs and how your therapy evolves. The goal is to better understand the difficulties you face, identify their causes, and build lasting change.
practicePage.imageAlt: Cream armchairs and a wooden bookshelf in a bright room, consultation room atmosphere

modalities.title: Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT)
modalities.description: Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT) looks at how thoughts, emotions and behaviours interact. Certain ways of thinking or reacting can, without our being aware of it, maintain the difficulties we face. By shedding light on these mechanisms and offering concrete tools, CBT helps you gradually move out of these patterns and build responses better suited to everyday life.

modalities.title: Gestalt therapy
modalities.description: Gestalt therapy favours working in the here and now. It draws on lived experience, emotions, bodily sensations, and the quality of contact with yourself, others and your environment. This approach invites a more conscious presence to what is being experienced, and the chance to try new ways of relating to others.

modalities.title: Schema therapy
modalities.description: Schema therapy explores the patterns that form over the course of a life, particularly in childhood, and that continue to influence emotions, behaviours or relationships. By identifying their origin and their impact in the present, it allows outdated patterns to evolve and new, more adapted bearings to gradually take hold.

modalities.title: Jungian psychology
modalities.description: Jungian psychology offers a complementary perspective on the difficulties you face. Its aim is to gradually bring certain unconscious processes into awareness — processes that shape how we think, feel and act. By fostering deeper self-knowledge, this approach supports the process of individuation: the development of the personality toward a way of functioning that is more conscious, coherent, and true to oneself.

journey.title: My background and training
paragraphs: After fifteen years spent understanding and responding to the specific needs of my clients, I chose to dedicate myself to therapeutic work.
My training in CBT, Gestalt therapy, Schema Therapy and Jungian psychology now feeds into an integrative practice, adapted to each person and their situation.

firstSession.title: The first session
paragraphs: The first session is a time to meet and talk.

It allows us to better understand what brings you here, to talk through your background, answer your questions, and decide together whether this approach fits what you are looking for. If so, we define the details of the therapy together.
